# ruler -- one row per succession.
#
# Replaces balance_ruler_slots_effects.txt, which spelled out 22,621 numbered
# slots so that a row could be addressed without an array index. A global
# variable map is keyed by a runtime number, so the index the language was
# missing is available after all: the row counter is the key and each column is
# its own map. The bucket walk, the slot ceiling and the generated file all go.
#
# Read from the save under `variables.map_data`, one container per column:
#
#     map_data={ { name="ruler_ctry"
#                  list={ { key={ type=value identity=<row * 100000> }
#                           value={ ... } } ... } } }
#
# Keys are the row number and come back in no particular order -- sort by key.
# Numbers carry the usual x100000 scale. Rows are paired across columns by key,
# so column A's key 7 and column B's key 7 are the same row.
#
# Columns (4), each a map of its own:
#     ctry     <- root
#     old      <- scope:old_ruler
#     new      <- scope:new_ruler
#     end      <- current_date
#
# global_var:ruler_count is still the row count and still the last key written.

ruler_increment_and_log = {
	if = {
		limit = { NOT = { has_global_variable = ruler_count } }
		set_global_variable = { name = ruler_count value = 0 }
	}
	change_global_variable = { name = ruler_count add = 1 }

	add_to_global_variable_map = { name = ruler_ctry key = global_var:ruler_count value = root }
	add_to_global_variable_map = { name = ruler_old key = global_var:ruler_count value = scope:old_ruler }
	add_to_global_variable_map = { name = ruler_new key = global_var:ruler_count value = scope:new_ruler }
	add_to_global_variable_map = { name = ruler_end key = global_var:ruler_count value = current_date }
}
